title: Breaking change in dependency type inspection in FastAPI 0.123.7
body:

First Check

 I added a very descriptive title here.
 I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
 I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search.
 I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information.

 I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to Pydantic.
 I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to Swagger UI.
 I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to ReDoc.

Commit to Help

 I commit to help with one of those options 👆

Example Code
# /// script
# requires-python = "==3.14.*"
# dependencies = [
#   "fastapi==0.123.7",
#   "uvicorn",
# ]
# ///

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator

app = FastAPI()


class DummyClient:
    async def get_people(self) -> list:
        return ["John Doe", "Jane Doe"]

    async def close(self) -> None: ...


async def get_client() -> AsyncGenerator[DummyClient, None]:
    client = DummyClient()
    yield client
    await client.close()


Client = Annotated[DummyClient, Depends(get_client)]


@app.get("/")
async def get_people(client: Client) -> list:
    return await client.get_people()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8000)
Description
This code works under FastAPI < 0.123.7, but fails with newer releases:
traceback

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/project/fastapi-nameerror/main.py", line 37, in <module>
    @app.get("/")
     ~~~~~~~^^^^^
  File "/project/fastapi-nameerror/.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/fastapi/routing.py", line 1072, in decorator
    self.add_api_route(
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^
        path,
        ^^^^^
    ...<23 lines>...
        generate_unique_id_function=generate_unique_id_function,
        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    )
    ^
  File "/project/fastapi-nameerror/.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/fastapi/routing.py", line 1011, in add_api_route
    route = route_class(
        self.prefix + path,
    ...<24 lines>...
        generate_unique_id_function=current_generate_unique_id,
    )
  File "/project/fastapi-nameerror/.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/fastapi/routing.py", line 630, in __init__
    self.dependant = get_dependant(
                     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~^
        path=self.path_format, call=self.endpoint, scope="function"
        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    )
    ^
  File "/project/fastapi-nameerror/.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py", line 290, in get_dependant
    sub_dependant = get_dependant(
        path=path,
    ...<5 lines>...
        scope=param_details.depends.scope,
    )
  File "/project/fastapi-nameerror/.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py", line 259, in get_dependant
    endpoint_signature = get_typed_signature(call)
  File "/project/fastapi-nameerror/.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py", line 196, in get_typed_signature
    signature = inspect.signature(call, eval_str=True)
  File "/Users/edgarramirez/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.14.0-macos-aarch64-none/lib/python3.14/inspect.py", line 3312, in signature
    return Signature.from_callable(obj, follow_wrapped=follow_wrapped,
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
                                   globals=globals, locals=locals, eval_str=eval_str,

Additional Context
Moving the AsyncGenerator outside of the type-checking block does fix the issue but it still seems like a breaking change was inadvertently introduced in a patch version.
  from __future__ import annotations

+ from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
- from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Annotated
+ from typing import Annotated

  from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI

- if TYPE_CHECKING:
-     from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
Note: seems like #11355 introduced the change.

answer.body:
Thanks for the very simple replicable example @edgarrmondragon! :rocket: 

I used it in the tests.

I created an issue here for completeness: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/issues/14484

This should be solved by https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/14485

It's available in FastAPI 0.124.2, just released :tada:
